chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Aban, from Hukeym who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the least of atheism (disbelief), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Arrogance is the least of it'.

key_terms.الْإِلْحَادِ: Atheism or divergence from the truth

ai.seo_question: What is the smallest form of atheism or divergence from truth according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the minimal threshold of *al-ilhad* (divergence or straying) as *al-kibr* (arrogance), highlighting that even subtle self-importance constitutes a fundamental departure from divine truth. This definition is significant in Shia theology as it links the spiritual disease of pride directly to the root of disbelief, suggesting that arrogance is the gateway through which one moves from faith to deviation. The hadith serves as a practical diagnostic tool for believers to identify the earliest signs of spiritual decline in their character.
